questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code discards repeated or superseded location updates? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.

A driver's app crashes and restarts mid-shift. The new process starts a new session and numbers its pings from 1 again, while the stored mark for that driver has sequence 4812. What happens to the first ping of the new session?
choices: It is dropped as OUT_OF_ORDER because 1 is lower than 4812
It is dropped as a DUPLICATE because the driver id was already seen
It is held back until the sequence passes 4812
It is accepted, because the session start is later than the stored one, and the mark is replaced

questions.prompt: Why is the comparison done inside marks.asMap().compute(...) rather than a get followed by a put?
choices: compute applies the lookup and the replacement for one driver atomically, so two threads cannot both accept the same sequence
compute makes Caffeine write the new mark to every node in the cluster
compute extends the expiry of the entry beyond expireAfterAccess
get and put are not allowed on a Caffeine cache

questions.prompt: When positions.upsertLatest throws, the listener calls filter.forget(...) and rethrows. What does the forget accomplish?
choices: It frees memory so the failed driver cannot cause the cache to exceed its maximum size
When the batch is redelivered, the failed update is evaluated afresh instead of being rejected as a DUPLICATE of a mark that was recorded but never persisted
It tells Kafka to skip the failed record on redelivery
It prevents the other drivers in the batch from being processed twice
